coverage: All fifteen scenes in both original-en and modern-en: named cast, speaking and stage roles, scene-local servants and lords, and the classical and religious figures named in the play.

entities.name: Leontes
entities.body: The King of Sicilia, Hermione’s husband and Mamillius’s father.

entities.name: Hermione
entities.body: Leontes’s queen, Mamillius’s mother, and pregnant as the play opens.

snapshots.body: Leontes’s queen, alive after sixteen years, coming down from the pedestal where she stood as her own statue.

entities.name: Polixenes
entities.body: The King of Bohemia, Leontes’s friend since boyhood and Florizel’s father.

snapshots.body: The King of Bohemia, at his son’s sheep-shearing feast in disguise.

entities.name: Paulina
entities.body: A lady of Hermione’s court and Antigonus’s wife, plain-spoken to the King’s face.

entities.name: Camillo
entities.body: A Sicilian lord in Leontes’s confidence.

snapshots.body: The Sicilian lord who has fled to Bohemia with Polixenes and entered his service.
Polixenes’s Bohemian counsellor, at the sheep-shearing in disguise beside his king.

entities.name: Perdita
entities.body: Leontes and Hermione’s newborn daughter, whom Antigonus names as he leaves her.

snapshots.body: Leontes and Hermione’s lost daughter, grown up in Bohemia and taken for the old Shepherd’s child.
Leontes and Hermione’s daughter, known now at her father’s court in Sicilia.

entities.name: Florizel
entities.body: Polixenes’s son, prince of Bohemia.

snapshots.body: Polixenes’s son, courting Perdita at the feast under the name Doricles.
Polixenes’s son, escaping Bohemia in the clothes he has taken from Autolycus.

entities.name: Autolycus
entities.body: A pedlar, ballad-seller and pickpocket on the Bohemian roads, once in Prince Florizel’s service.

entities.name: The old Shepherd
entities.body: The Bohemian shepherd who finds the abandoned child on the shore.

snapshots.body: The Bohemian shepherd who found the child, made a gentleman at the Sicilian court.

entities.name: The Clown
entities.body: The old Shepherd’s son.

snapshots.body: The old Shepherd’s son, made a gentleman at the Sicilian court.

entities.name: Antigonus
entities.body: A Sicilian lord and Paulina’s husband.

entities.name: Mamillius
entities.body: Leontes and Hermione’s young son, prince of Sicilia.

entities.name: Time
entities.body: Time as Chorus, who carries the play across the sixteen years between its halves.

entities.name: Archidamus
entities.body: A Bohemian lord attending Polixenes on his visit to Sicilia.

entities.name: Cleomenes
entities.body: A Sicilian lord sent with Dion to consult Apollo’s oracle at Delphos.

entities.name: Dion
entities.body: A Sicilian lord sent with Cleomenes to consult Apollo’s oracle at Delphos.

entities.name: Emilia
entities.body: A lady attending Hermione.

entities.name: Mopsa
entities.body: A shepherdess at the sheep-shearing, courted by the Clown.

entities.name: Dorcas
entities.body: A shepherdess at the sheep-shearing, and Mopsa’s rival for the Clown.

entities.name: The First Lord
entities.body: A lord of Leontes’s court in Sicilia.

entities.name: The lord
entities.body: A lord attending Leontes sixteen years later.

entities.name: The First Lady
entities.body: A lady attending Hermione and Mamillius.

entities.name: The Second Lady
entities.body: A lady attending Hermione and Mamillius.

entities.name: The First Attendant
entities.body: An attendant on Leontes.

entities.name: The officer of the court
entities.body: The officer who reads the indictment and the oracle at Hermione’s trial.

entities.name: The Gaoler
entities.body: The keeper of the prison where Hermione is held.

entities.name: The Mariner
entities.body: The seaman who lands Antigonus on the Bohemian coast.

entities.name: Leontes’s servant
entities.body: A servant of Leontes’s household in Sicilia.

entities.name: The servant at the trial
entities.body: The servant who brings Leontes word of his son.

entities.name: The Shepherd’s servant
entities.body: The servant who announces the pedlar at the sheep-shearing.

entities.name: The servant at the Sicilian court
entities.body: A servant of Leontes’s household sixteen years later.

entities.name: The First Gentleman
entities.body: A gentleman of the Sicilian court who saw the kings meet.

entities.name: Rogero
entities.body: A gentleman of the Sicilian court, named Rogero.

entities.name: The Third Gentleman
entities.body: Paulina’s steward, who describes the reunion.

entities.name: The lords
entities.body: The lords of the Sicilian and Bohemian courts.

entities.name: The ladies
entities.body: The ladies attending Hermione.

entities.name: The officers
entities.body: The officers of the court at Hermione’s trial.

entities.name: The guards
entities.body: The guards attending the trial.

entities.name: The attendants
entities.body: The attendants on the two kings.

entities.name: The shepherds and shepherdesses
entities.body: The country people at the sheep-shearing feast.

entities.name: The satyrs
entities.body: The twelve herdsmen who dance a satyrs’ dance at the feast.

entities.name: The Emperor of Russia
entities.body: Hermione’s father, whom she calls on at her trial; the play gives him no name.

entities.name: Julio Romano
entities.body: The Italian master said to have made the statue of Hermione.

entities.name: Mistress Taleporter
entities.body: The midwife named as a witness in one of Autolycus’s ballads.

entities.name: Smalus
entities.body: The Libyan king Florizel falsely claims as the father of his bride.

entities.name: Alexander the Great
entities.body: The Macedonian king, cited by Cleomenes on leaving a crown to the worthiest.

entities.name: Judas
entities.body: The disciple who betrayed Christ, named by Polixenes as the worst company for a name.

entities.name: Deucalion
entities.body: The survivor of the flood in Greek myth, a byword for the remotest ancestry.

entities.name: Apollo
entities.body: The god whose oracle at Delphos answers Leontes.

entities.name: Jove
entities.body: The Roman king of the gods, also called Jupiter here.

entities.name: Jupiter
entities.body: Jove under his other name, in Florizel’s list of gods who took animal shapes.

entities.name: Neptune
entities.body: The god of the sea.

entities.name: Phoebus
entities.body: The sun god.

entities.name: Mercury
entities.body: The god of thieves, whom Autolycus claims as his birth-star.

entities.name: Juno
entities.body: The queen of the gods, invoked for the whiteness of her hands.

entities.name: Cytherea
entities.body: Venus under her island name, in Perdita’s catalogue of flowers.

entities.name: Flora
entities.body: The goddess of flowers, whom Florizel says Perdita resembles at the feast.

entities.name: Proserpina
entities.body: The goddess carried off by Dis, whose scattered flowers Perdita names.

entities.name: Dis
entities.body: The god of the underworld, who carried Proserpina away in his waggon.

entities.name: The Fates
entities.body: The powers who spin and cut the thread of a life.
